brief_summary: Hero art for the Trends pillar piece on TMR (tunnel-magnetoresistance) switches climbing on the trend tracker for five straight weeks (W38 to W42, scores roughly 55 to 90). A five-point sparkline climbs left to right across the whole canvas in the splash hue, with a small muted magnetic-switch cross-section (stem, magnet, sensing gap, sensor pad on the PCB) kept secondary at upper left per the brief's optional technical-motif pairing.
source: plan/bearings.md section Article hero art, colorful keyboard SVGs (locked 2026-05-09), trends piece maps to sparkline silhouette
template: directive: simple line drawing + single splash of color illustrative of subject; trends piece -> sparkline silhouette, optionally paired with a secondary technical motif (cf. cherry-xtrfy-tmr-pivot.svg)
subject: A five-point sparkline (W38 through W42) climbing left to right, rendered entirely in the splash hue rather than only at the terminus, since the five-week climb itself is the article's subject: interior points as filled dots, the W42 point enlarged with a halo ring plus a small trajectory chevron signaling the climb continues past the frame, and a low-opacity splash wash filling the area beneath the ascending line down to the baseline. A baseline axis with five per-week tick marks runs beneath the chart. At upper left, out of the sparkline's path, a small muted magnetic-switch cross-section (simplified single-volume housing, a stem descending to a splash-filled magnet, a dashed sensing gap, and a splash-filled sensor pad on a PCB line) sits at reduced group opacity so it reads as a supporting technical cue rather than the piece's subject.
stroke_weight: 2px (3px on the sparkline polyline itself, matching the family's emphasis convention for the focal trajectory, cf. cherry-tracker-slide-keychron-kickstarter-delivers.svg)
alt: A sparkline chart showing five weekly points climbing steadily upward from lower left to upper right in a dusty-rose color, with a small muted diagram of a magnetic switch cross-section, showing a stem, a magnet, and a sensor pad, in the upper left corner.
notes: Splash hue dusty rose chosen from the brief's allowed set {coral, dusty rose, ochre, muted terracotta}: this piece's closest TMR siblings already use coral (tmr-switches-deep-dive.svg, hue 24) and muted terracotta (cherry-xtrfy-tmr-pivot.svg, hue 40), and keychron-q16-he-8k-ceramic-tmr.svg uses ochre (hue 85), so dusty rose keeps this piece visually distinct within the TMR cluster. Value oklch(0.63 0.095 9) chosen to sit clear of the dusty-rose hues already in rotation across the broader corpus (12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20). All five data points are illustrative of an ascending five-week trend per the brief (W38 through W42, roughly 55 to 90); exact y-coordinates are a stylized smooth climb, not a pixel-literal plot, consistent with family convention for sparkline hero art (cf. cherry-tracker-slide-keychron-kickstarter-delivers.svg's own warning note on stylized interpolation). No rendered text anywhere in the file; the climb and the secondary switch motif carry the subject without labels, per family convention for the trends-pillar sparkline pieces. All XML comments use single-hyphen text only (no double-hyphen runs) per the svg-validity.test.ts regression guard at apps/web/src/__tests__/svg-validity.test.ts; verified locally with a minidom parse plus a manual double-hyphen scan, both clean.
data_sources: brief: TMR switches climbing on the trend tracker for five straight weeks, W38 to W42, scores roughly 55, 63, 71, 85, 90
